Mr.Anil Kumar Goyal, learned counsel for respondent No.
 Company.

ORDER The appellant has filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 21.02.2019 passed by learned XVIII Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) in Claim Case No.2300127/2015, whereby the appellant has challenged the quantum of compensation.
2. The liability of the Insurance Company is not in dispute.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 29.11.2012 at around 10:15 PM, appellant Mukul was going along with his friend Inder on a motorcycle as a pillion rider to Balgarh to attend marriage ceremony.
When they reached near Ganga Warehouse on the Indore-Bhopal Bypass, they stopped to answer call of nature.

At that time, a truck bearing registration number MP-09-KC-4645, which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner by its driver, dashed into the appellant causing him to sustain multiple injuries on various parts of his body.

His NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:31902 2 MA-2940-2019 jaw and right leg were fractured, his toes were also fractured and he sustained grievous injuries in head resulting in loss of memory.
3.1 He remained hospitalised from 30.11.2012 to 09.01.2013 at Bombay Hospital, Indore, where he underwent surgery.
He was again hospitalised in the same hospital from 10.02.2013 to 11.02.2013.
3.2 The appellant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the aforesaid accident.

The Claims Tribunal after Mukul Verma Through Guardian Chaganlal ... vs Manmohan Singh on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100295049/
1 recording evidence, concluded that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the insured vehicle, which resulted in injuries to the appellant.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the appellant was awarded total compensation of Rs.17,32,584/-.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Claims Tribunal while awarding compensation has considered the permanent disability of the appellant only to the extent of 70%, which considering the condition of the appellant should have been taken at 100%.
4.1 She further submits that considering the ongoing treatment required by the appellant, the Claims Tribunal should have awarded a separate amount towards future medical expenses.

4.2 She also points out that the Claims Tribunal has incorrectly assessed the income of the appellant at Rs.3,800/- per month, whereas the appellant had claimed that he was engaged in Emu farming and was earning Rs.5,00,000/- per annum therefrom.
4.3 Learned counsel for the appellant, therefore prays for enhancement of the compensation accordingly.

5 . Per contra , learned counsel for the Insurance Company points out that even the appellant's own witness deposed before the Claims Tribunal and issued a NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:31902 3 MA-2940-2019 certificate certifying that the appellant has suffered 60%
overall permanent disability.
However, after considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, the Claims Tribunal has taken the disability to be 70%.
Thus, the Tribunal has awarded just and proper compensation, in which no interference is warranted.
He, therefore, prays for dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
7.

From perusal of Ex. P-261, the permanent disability certificate and the statement of Dr. Aproov Puranik, who has certified the overall permanent disability of the appellant at 60%, this Court is of the considered view that the Tribunal has correctly assessed the permanent disability of the appellate at 70%.
8.

As regards the income of the appellant, it is seen that the Tribunal did not believe the claim made by the appellant that he was earning Rs.5,00,000/- per annum, in the absence of any supporting material in this regard.
This Court has also perused the record of the Claims Tribunal and has not found any substantive material to demonstrate that the appellant was earning Rs.5,00,000/- per annum.
Hence, no interference is warranted with respect to the conclusion of the Claims Tribunal in disbelieving the appellant's claim regarding his income.
However, it is seen that the Claims Tribunal has notionally taken the income of the appellant at Rs.3,800/- per month without there being any reference material to support the same.

9. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Hans Raj vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., passed in SLP (C)
No.3511 of 2020 has held that in the absence of material to establish the income of the injured,

10. A perusal of the said guidelines shows that at the relevant time i.e. on 29.11.2012, the minimum wages for an unskilled labourer were Rs.4,945/-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:31902 4 MA-2940-2019 .
Accordingly, the same is taken as the income of the appellant on the date of the accident.

11. Considering the fact that the appellant is still suffering from the injuries and is undergoing treatment, this Court is of the considered view that a further amount deserves to be added to the compensation which is to be awarded after the enhancement of the income of the appellant.
12. As such, after calculating the compensation, the differential amount comes to Rs.2,43,373/-.

However, a further addition is made towards future treatment and other heads, this amount is qualified at lump sum of Rs.3,00,000/- which shall be paid to the appellant over and above the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application before the Claims Tribunal.
13. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed off.
